evidence: R01-F01 is remediated by resolving one UUIDv7 actor from the current Windows user's DPAPI-protected profile vault. Missing or corrupt actor authority fails closed before project persistence, and inbound actor assertion headers are denied as spoof attempts.

The exact same non-null actor ID and human type are carried into every immutable revision and its append-only provenance fact. Restart and successive revision tests prove the identity is stable; no institutional or remote identity is claimed.

Schema v6 is a forward-only, backup-first migration that widens only provenance actor authority to retained canonical identifiers or UUIDv7. It preserves rows, reinstalls the exact append-only triggers/index, records immutable migration history, and supports every exact v1-v5 source.

R01-F02 is remediated by requiring the public idempotency key and binding it to the manifest project, stable actor, canonical command digest, domain project, immutable revision digest, provenance event, and outbox event in the same transaction.

Replay is checked before optimistic-revision rejection and again under BEGIN IMMEDIATE. An identical retry before or after restart returns the original immutable projection; changed project, actor, or command reuse is denied, and a genuinely new stale command retains the normal revision conflict.

Adversarial tests prove two competing identical writers converge on exactly one revision, one binding, one provenance event, and one outbox row, while malformed authority and persistence failure roll back all four surfaces.

Core API, repository port/adapter, Windows composition, OpenAPI/generated client, portable storage profile, migration-recovery contract, documentation, and Windows/data/service/security tests changed together at exact candidate a60d3e9704a4d59dd1d0310437bd6d486057500b.
The immutable R01 submission and review ledger remain ancestral and both blocking finding IDs are replayed explicitly for independent closure.

The remediation introduces no cloud, institutional identity, dependency, governed UI reference, downstream workflow policy, or release claim. Those approved dependent-task and W1-exit duties remain unchanged.
